The local types in the behavior pool handle the actual event raising:

ABAPCLASS lcl_event_handler DEFINITION FRIENDS ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBER.
  PUBLIC SECTION.
    CLASS-METHODS on_created IMPORTING it_events TYPE ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBER=>tt_created.
    CLASS-METHODS on_changed IMPORTING it_events TYPE ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBER=>tt_changed.
    CLASS-METHODS on_deleted IMPORTING it_events TYPE ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBER=>tt_deleted.
ENDCLASS.

CLASS lcl_event_handler IMPLEMENTATION.
  METHOD on_created.
    RAISE ENTITY EVENT ZR_BPTAXNUMBER~Created FROM it_events.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD on_changed.
    RAISE ENTITY EVENT ZR_BPTAXNUMBER~Changed FROM it_events.
  ENDMETHOD.
  METHOD on_deleted.
    RAISE ENTITY EVENT ZR_BPTAXNUMBER~Deleted FROM it_events.
  ENDMETHOD.
ENDCLASS.

 

Step 3 – Configure the Event Binding and Channel

Once the RAP events exist, they must be wired to an outbound channel in the Enterprise Event Enablement Fiori app.

Event Binding – Z_BPTAXNUM

Create one Event Binding per event. The binding links the RAP entity event to an event type in the CloudEvents format:

Field Value
Type Namespaceoneerp
SAP Object TypeTaxNumber
Operationchanged
Typeoneerp.TaxNumber.changed.v*

The Event Version entry maps the RAP entity ZR_BPTAXNUMBER and entity event CHANGED to major version 0001.

 

Channel – Outbound Binding Configuration

A Channel is created once per event broker. After activating the channel (e.g. AEM_BROKER), the Outbound Bindings view shows all topics that will be published, including the newly created oneerp/TaxNumber/changed/v1/{xsaptaxtype} topic.

Step 4 – Create the Custom BOR Object (SWO1)

The trigger mechanism relies on a BOR object that represents the Tax Number entity. Use transaction SWO1 to create it.

Create Object Type ZTAXNUM

Field Value
Object TypeZTAXNUM
Object nameZTAXNUM
NameTaxNumber
ProgramZRBUS1006_TAXNUMBER
ApplicationF

 

BOR Object Structure

After creation, add the following to the object type:

  • Key fields: ZTAXNUM.PARTNER (Business Partner Number), ZTAXNUM.TAXTYPE (Tax Number Category)
  • Attributes: ZTAXNUM.ObjectType, ZTAXNUM.TaxNumber
  • Methods: ZTAXNUM.ExistenceCheck, ZTAXNUM.Display
  • Events: ZTAXNUM.TaxNumberChanged, ZTAXNUM.TaxNumberDeleted, ZTAXNUM.TaxNumberCreated

Set the object type to status "Implemented" and generate it.

 

Step 5 – Understand the Trigger Mechanism

The Change Document Flag

The trigger relies on SAP's Change Document infrastructure. The data element BPTAXNUM (Business Partner Tax Number) has the "Change Document" flag set in its Further Characteristics tab.

This means that every time a Tax Number is created, changed, or deleted, a change document entry is written automatically to tables CDHDR and CDPOS.

 

Finding the Right Change Document Object

Table TCDOB lists which Change Document Objects cover which database tables. A search for table DFKKBPTAXNUM returns the Change Document Object MKK_BPTAX, confirming that this object tracks all Tax Number changes.

 

Step 6 – Wire the BOR Event to the Change Document (SWEC / SWED)

SWEC – Events for Change Documents

In transaction SWEC, link the Change Document Object to the BOR event:

Field Value
Change Doc. ObjectMKK_BPTAX
Object CategoryBOR Object Type
Object TypeZTAXNUM
EventTAXNUMBERCHANGED
Trigger EventOn Change

 

SWED – Change Document Object Declaration

In transaction SWED, declare the Change Document Object with its leading table. This entry tells the workflow engine the structure of the object key, so it can populate the event container correctly at runtime.

Field Value
Change Document ObjectMKK_BPTAX
Leading table in change documentDFKKBPTAXNUM
Change document key with structureDFKKBPTAXNUM
Action: Create / Change / DeleteAll checked

 

Step 7 – Create the Event Linkage Function Module (SWE2)

Transaction SWE2 (Event Type Linkages) connects the BOR event to a Receiver Function Module that will be called when the event fires.

SWE2 Configuration

Field Value
Object CategoryBOR Object Type
Object TypeZTAXNUM
EventTAXNUMBERCHANGED
Receiver TypeZAIF_EVENT
Receiver CallFunction Module
Receiver Function ModuleZAEM_RAP_EVENT_HANDLER
Event deliveryUsing tRFC (Default)
Linkage ActivatedYes

 

Function Module ZAEM_RAP_EVENT_HANDLER

This is the core bridge between the BOR world and the RAP event world. The function module:

  1. Reads the change number (CD_CHANGENR) from the event container
  2. Looks up CDPOS to find which Tax Number record changed
  3. Parses the composite TABKEY to extract BusinessPartner and TaxType
  4. Reads the current record from the API view A_BUSINESSPARTNERTAXNUMBER
  5. If the record was deleted: calls ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBER=>raise_deleted with the key only
  6. If the record still exists: calls ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBER=>raise_changed with the full payload
ABAPFUNCTION zaem_rap_event_handler
  IMPORTING
    VALUE(objtype) LIKE swetypecou-objtype
    VALUE(objkey)  LIKE sweinstcou-objkey
    VALUE(event)   LIKE sweinstcou-event
    VALUE(rectype) LIKE swetypecou-rectype
  TABLES
    event_container LIKE swcont.

  READ TABLE event_container ASSIGNING FIELD-SYMBOL(<ls_event_container>)
    WHERE element = 'CD_CHANGENR'.

  IF <ls_event_container> IS ASSIGNED.

    SELECT tabname, tabkey FROM cdpos UP TO 1 ROWS INTO @DATA(ls_tab)
      WHERE changenr = @<ls_event_container>-value
        AND tabname  = 'DFKKBPTAXNUM'.
    ENDSELECT.

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " DFKKBPTAXNUM key layout: MANDT(3) + PARTNER(10) + STCOTYPE(3)
    DATA(lv_business_partner) = ls_tab-tabkey+3(10).
    DATA(lv_tax_type)         = ls_tab-tabkey+13(3).

    SELECT SINGLE businesspartner, bptaxtype, bptaxnumber,
                  bptaxlongnumber, authorizationgroup
      FROM a_businesspartnertaxnumber
      INTO @DATA(ls_taxnum)
      WHERE businesspartner = @lv_business_partner
        AND bptaxtype       = @lv_tax_type.

    IF sy-subrc <> 0.
      " Record deleted — raise Deleted event with key only
      DATA lt_deleted TYPE zbp_r_bptaxnumber=>tt_deleted.
      APPEND VALUE #(
        %key = VALUE #(
          businesspartner = lv_business_partner
          bptaxtype       = lv_tax_type
        )
      ) TO lt_deleted.
      zbp_r_bptaxnumber=>raise_deleted( lt_deleted ).
      RETURN.
    ENDIF.

    " Record exists — raise Changed event with full payload
    DATA lt_changed TYPE zbp_r_bptaxnumber=>tt_changed.
    APPEND VALUE #(
      %key = VALUE #(
        businesspartner = ls_taxnum-businesspartner
        bptaxtype       = ls_taxnum-bptaxtype
      )
      %param = VALUE z_bptaxnum_evt_payload(
        taxtype            = ls_taxnum-bptaxtype
        bptaxnumber        = ls_taxnum-bptaxnumber
        bptaxlongnumber    = ls_taxnum-bptaxlongnumber
        authorizationgroup = ls_taxnum-authorizationgroup
      )
    ) TO lt_changed.
    zbp_r_bptaxnumber=>raise_changed( lt_changed ).

  ENDIF.

ENDFUNCTION.

 

Key implementation detail: The TABKEY in CDPOS is a concatenated string of all key fields of the changed table. For DFKKBPTAXNUM the layout is MANDT(3) + PARTNER(10) + STCOTYPE(3), so the Business Partner starts at offset 3 and the Tax Type at offset 13.

Step 8 – Verify in the Event Monitor

Use the Enterprise Event Enablement – Event Monitor Fiori app to verify that events are flowing to the broker.

After changing a Tax Number for Business Partner 161, the monitor shows multiple events published to the topic S/4HANA/Events/ce/oneerp/TaxNumber/changed/v1/{xsaptaxtype}. The dynamic segment {xsaptaxtype} is resolved to the actual tax type (e.g. /DE2).

The CloudEvents JSON payload looks like this:

JSON{
  "type": "oneerp.TaxNumber.changed.v1",
  "specversion": "1.0",
  "source": "/default/sap.s4.custom/T33CLNT800",
  "id": "fa163e75-aaba-1fd1-a0bf-b0d5fb23e000",
  "time": "2026-07-17T18:35:31Z",
  "xsaptaxtype": "DE2",
  "datacontenttype": "application/json",
  "data": {
    "BusinessPartner": "161",
    "BPTaxType": "DE2",
    "TaxType": "DE2",
    "BPTaxNumber": "2",
    "BPTaxLongNumber": "",
    "AuthorizationGroup": ""
  }
}

 

Step 9 – Test with AEM Try-Me

In the AEM web console, use the Try Me tab to subscribe to the topic and verify message reception end-to-end.

Subscribe to S/4HANA/Events/ce/oneerp/TaxNumber/changed/v1/DE2 (or use wildcards). After triggering a Tax Number change in S/4HANA, the message appears immediately in the Messages panel with the CloudEvents envelope and the full data payload.

 

Summary

This pattern requires the following development objects:

Object Type Purpose
ZR_BPTAXNUMBERCDS Root View EntityRAP business object anchor
Z_BPTAXNUM_EVT_PAYLOADCDS Abstract EntityEvent payload structure
ZBP_R_BPTAXNUMBERABAP Behavior Poolraise_* helper methods + RAISE ENTITY EVENT
Z_BPTAXNUMEvent BindingMaps RAP event to CloudEvents topic
ZTAXNUMBOR Object TypeCustom BOR object with key fields and events
ZAEM_RAP_EVENT_HANDLERFunction ModuleBridges BOR event to RAP event
SWEC entryConfigurationLinks MKK_BPTAX change docs to ZTAXNUM.TAXNUMBERCHANGED
SWED entryConfigurationDeclares MKK_BPTAX object and key structure
SWE2 entryConfigurationRoutes BOR event to the function module

Trade-offs

Cons

  • Data selection and mapping to the event payload must be coded individually for each event type — this is the highest-effort part.

Pros

  • Events fire only when a Tax Number actually changes — no polling, no scheduling.
  • No additional CPI flow is needed on the consumer side.
  • No extra persistence is needed; SAP's change document infrastructure (CDPOS) already tracks every change reliably.

Extensibility

The same pattern applies to any BOR-managed object that writes change documents. To add a Created or Deleted event, add a corresponding SWEC entry with trigger On Create / On Delete and extend ZAEM_RAP_EVENT_HANDLER to handle those cases.

If multiple consumers are interested in Business Partner data beyond Tax Numbers, consider a complementary approach using the standard BusinessPartner.Changed RAP event as a trigger, combined with a CPI flow that reads the specific data via OData API — avoiding the need for one custom BOR object per sub-entity.

entry.title: I tried the SAC Lite Viewer — and my story didn't even qualify
entry.content:
In the comments on my last performance write-up, a fellow member made a valuable point: before optimizing render times widget by widget, try the Lite Viewer. It decouples the viewer from the designer persona and can significantly cut the client-side load — targeting exactly the frontend cost I had been measuring, not the backend.

I promised a follow-up. Here it is — and it didn't go the way I expected, which is precisely why it's worth sharing.

What I expected vs. what happened

My plan was simple: open my story in view mode, confirm it ran through the Lite Viewer, and compare the render behavior against my earlier numbers.

The catch: the Lite Viewer is not a button you press. SAP Analytics Cloud switches to it automatically when a story is eligible — and silently falls back to the full Optimized (Unified) experience when it isn't. No error, no warning. So "run the Lite Viewer" really means "make the story eligible, open it, and then verify which viewer actually served it."

To verify, I didn't rely on feel. I checked the tenant telemetry in System Overview, under Opened Stories per Story Version:

  • Light Weight Viewer: — (no opens)
  • Unified Story: 1 (my open landed here)

The verdict is unambiguous: my story did not go through the Lite Viewer. It fell back to the full Unified Story experience.

Why it didn't qualify

The reason is the one hinted at in that comment thread. My story sits on a Planning model. As soon as SAP Analytics Cloud sees a Planning context, it routes the story to the Unified Story experience rather than the Lite Viewer. Planning-capable content and the Lite Viewer don't mix — the viewer is designed for lightweight, view-only consumption.

So the render savings I was hoping to measure were never on the table for this story. Not because the Lite Viewer doesn't work, but because the story was never a candidate for it.

What it actually takes to qualify

From working through this, here is the short list I'd check before expecting the Lite Viewer to kick in:

  1. Optimized (Unified) story experience — not Classic.
  2. No Planning or advanced BI features. A Planning model is enough on its own to disqualify the story. For a rolling forecast like mine, that means building a report-only variant on a non-Planning (Analytics) model if you want it to qualify.
  3. New Table Experience for tables. A classic table quietly drops the story out of Lite Viewer eligibility.

The theme across all three: eligibility is decided by the content, not by a setting you flip. And because the fallback is silent, telemetry (System Overview) is the only reliable way to know which viewer really served your story.

Takeaway

If your story is for consumers rather than designers, check Lite Viewer eligibility early — ideally before you invest in per-widget render tuning. In my case the honest result is: this story never qualified, so the Lite Viewer couldn't help it. The next step, when I can rebuild on an Analytics model, is to run a report-only variant through it and measure the real difference — I'll post that comparison when I have it.

A fair caveat: this ran on a trial tenant, and the point here is the routing behavior (which viewer served the story), not an absolute render benchmark — my connection that day was slow enough that timing numbers wouldn't mean much anyway.

Thanks to whoever pointed me to the Lite Viewer — this is exactly the kind of follow-up the comment deserved, even when the answer turned out to be "it didn't qualify."

entry.title: Getting started with Micro-Integrations on Advanced Event Mesh: Access Options & Activation
entry.content:
Not every integration scenario requires a full-fledged integration platform. For some scenarios, all you need is a lightweight way to connect an application or service directly to your event broker.

This is where the Micro-Integrations capability of SAP Integration Suite, advanced Event Mesh comes in.
They provide lightweight integration functionality to easily connect SaaS and legacy applications, LLMs and AI Agents, messaging services, data stores, file servers, etc. directly to your event brokers. It also supports basic transformations, comparable to message mappings.

The keyword here is lightweight. Micro-Integrations are not a replacement for Cloud Integration, it complements it. Cloud Integration is designed to handle integration complexity way beyond the level that the Micro-Integrations capability can handle. Micro-Integrations focus on simplicity, speed, and high volume use cases.

In practice, using Cloud Integration for simple pass-through scenarios from or to Advanced Event Mesh with no transformation (apart from perhaps a message mapping) can be inefficient. In high-volume scenarios (e.g. Event Streaming) it means you’re consuming a lot of messages without leveraging the true strength of Cloud Integration.
This is exactly where the Micro-Integrations capability adds value: handling lightweight, high-throughput integrations, closer to the event broker, while leaving the more complex transformations to Cloud Integration.

The following blog: Small but Great: Introducing Micro-Integrations for Advanced Event Mesh was published when Micro-Integrations were released and provides more background on the capability. I recommend reading it before continuing this blog, as it explains the capability and benefits in more detail, this blog focuses specifically on how to obtain access.

Initially, included with certain broker service classes (as from Broker 1K), now they are also available an an additional chargeable capability. This new metric you can be charged for each hour an additional Micro-Integration is in state "deployed", the pricing can be found on SAP Discovery Center.

The following table shows how many Micro-Integrations (MI) are included with each broker service class, note that each MI can contain up to 5 flows:

Service ClassNr. of Micro-Integrations Included
Broker 100 (Developer)0
Broker 250 (Smallest Production Broker)0
Broker 1K2
Broker 5K5
Broker 10K8
Broker 50K15
Broker 100K25


This new (Micro-Integration by the hour) metric enables organizations to:

  1. Leverage Micro-Integrations when they only have small brokers:
    We recommend having the same broker size for PROD and QA. This means that for a 3 tier environment the smallest setup is Broker 250 for PROD and QA and Broker 100 for DEV. In this case, Micro-Integrations are not included in your broker and if you want to use Micro-Integrations, you need to purchase it as a seperate line item.

  2. Use additional flows:
    Every Micro-Integration comes with 5 flows, a single flow contains the details of a target/source system/queue/topic, error handling config (e.g. Dead Message Queues) and a message mapping.
    So let's say, you have an SFTP source micro-integration, these flows can listen to their own SFTP server or directory/folder and map different objects, for example:
    • 5 flows that listen to the same SFTP server but each to a different directory.
      One listens to the directory /salesorders and maps sales order objects, another one that listens to /businesspartners and maps business partner objects, etc:
      in this case you require 1 Micro-Integration.
    • 5 flows that each listen to a different SFTP server but they both map and publish sales order objects:
      in this case you require 1 Micro-Integration
    • 10 flows that listen to the same SFTP server, but map different objects:
      in this case you require 2 Micro-Integrations
     
  3. Leverage more Micro-Integrations than included in your Broker or Subaccount:
    Micro-Integrations cannot be shared across Subaccounts, so let's say you have a 3 tier environment with a 1K Broker in PROD & QA and a 250 Broker (no MIs included) in DEV, each environment is hosted in a different SAP BTP Subaccount. In this case, you can leverage 2 Micro-Integrations in PROD, 2 in QA (as this is included in your Broker), but if you were to use Micro-Integrations on your DEV Subaccount, you would need to activate the entitlement for additional Micro-Integrations on your DEV Subaccount.
    Following the same example, if you want to use more than 2 Micro-Integrations in your PROD and/or QA environment, you also need to activate the entitlement for additional MIs on your PROD and/or QA Subaccount.


In this blog, we will walk you through the process of enabling the Micro-Integrations add-on within your SAP AEM environment, as well as the activation process of a 1K Broker or larger.

Assigning the entitlements to your SAP BTP Subaccount

In this first part of the blog, we will assign the required entitlements to the SAP BTP Subaccount. Depending on how you want to obtain Micro-Integrations, this can either be the entitlement for the Micro-Integration add-on or an entitlement for a broker service class that includes Micro-Integrations (Broker 1K or larger).
This part of the process needs to be done by the Subaccount or Global Account Administrator on SAP Business Technology Platform.

  1. Go to your SAP BTP Cockpit
  2. Navigate to the SAP BTP Subaccount, where you have deployed an Advanced Event Mesh environment and where you want to enable Micro-Integrations.

     

  3. In your Subaccount, go to "Entitlements", and click on "Edit".

     

  4. Now, click on "Add Service Plan" on the right top of the table.
  5. Look for "integration-suite-advanced-event-mesh". 
  6. Now you should see "SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh", under "Services available to this subaccount", select this service.

     

  7. Under "Available Plans", select "micro-integration-add-on". This entitlement allows you to create additional Micro-Integrations beyond those included with eligible broker service classes.
  8. Optional: If you want to use the Micro-Integratoins included with your broker service, select the appropriate broker entitlement instead. For example, a Broker 1K includes two Micro-Integrations (this is smallest broker that includes MIs) , please have a look at the documentation if you want to know how many Micro-Integrations are included in your broker.
    You can also assign both entitlements if you want to use the Micro-Integrations included with your broker service and additional Micro-Integrations through the add-on.

     

  9. Once you've selected the right service plans, click on "Add Service Plans" at the bottom of your screen.

     

  10. Don't forget to press the "Save" button.

     

     

Optional: Ensure a compatible broker is available

To deploy Micro-Integrations, you need at least one active broker in your Advanced Event Mesh environment. If you are using the Micro-Integrations included with a broker service, the minimum service class is Broker 1K. If you are using the micro-integration-add-on entitlement, any broker service class can be used. This section is written for organizations that want to deploy a broker that already includes Micro-Integration. The following steps are performed by the Mission Control Manager in SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh.

  1. In your SAP BTP Subaccount, go to "Instances and Subscription" and open "SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh" (under "Subscriptions").

     

  2. Now, you are redirected to what we refer to as the “Cloud Console” in Advanced Event Mesh (you can always go back to the cloud console by clicking on the SAP logo on the top left).
  3. In the Cloud Console, scroll down to "Mission control" and open "Cluster Manager".

     

  4. In the Cluster Manager you seee an overview of your existing brokers. If you don't have a 1K Broker or a larger broker, click on "Create Service" on the right top.
  5. Provide at least the following:
    • Service Name
    • Cloud provider & region
    • Service Type: Enterprise
    • Service Class: Broker 1K (or larger)
  6. Click on "Create Service". 

     

  7. Once the service is ready, you should see a screen that looks like this (see screenshot below). This means that your broker was successfully created!

Granting access to Micro-Integrations

If you (or your admin) have successfully configured the appropriate Micro-Integration entitlement and/or broker service, we're almost ready to create and deploy Micro-Integrations. The only thing you must verify is that you and/or the people who should create and deploy the MIs, have the "Micro-Integrations Manager" role assigned. This part of the process is done by the Account Administrator in SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh.

  1. In the Cloud Console, click on the user icon (bottom left corner) and go to "Account Details".
  2. Now, go to "User Management" ➡️ "Users", click on the 3 dots right next to the user you want to grant access to Micro-Integrations and hit "Edit".

     

  3. Go to the line "Micro-Integrations" and open the drop-down list, select "Micro-Integrations Manager", and press "Save". Now this user will be able to create and deploy Micro-Integrations in SAP Integration Suite, advanced event mesh. Repeat the previous 3 steps to give access to other users.

     

Discovering and creating Micro-Integrations

Once the appropriate entitlement has been assigned, a compatible broker is available, and the Micro-Integrations Manager role has been assigned to your user, you can create and deploy Micro-Integrations.

  1. In the Cloud Console in Advanced Event Mesh, you should now see a tile with the title "Micro-Integrations". Click on this tile.

     

  2. Here, you will find an overview of all Micro-Integrations that are created. Click on "Create Micro-Integration" on the right top.

     

  3. Now, you see an overview of all Micro-Integrations that you can create and configure with Advanced Event Mesh.

     

  4. From this list, you can select a Micro-Integration that fits your use case and start configuring it. Configuring a Micro-Integration is very straight forward, you need the connection and credential details of the source or target system, as well as the queue/topic and broker credentials to create and configure the Micro-Integration.

If you want to try-out a Micro-Integration, I recommend to go through a blog I wrote earlier this year:
File to Mesh: Liberating SFTP Data with Micro-Integrations. 
In this blog, we create a Micro-Integration that listens to an SFTP server and publishes the lines of a CSV file one by one as (mapped) events to the broker. The File to Mesh use case is one where Micro-Integrations are commonly used.
